title: Balancing Flavor and Texture in Dairy-Free Vanilla Ice Cream (Merle)
summary: This Goodful video with Merle presents a dairy-free vanilla ice cream developed around a coconut-based vegan base. The host emphasizes the central challenge of balancing texture (creamy, solid mouthfeel) with flavor (vanilla notes) when dairy is absent, noting that coconut-derived components impart a strong flavor and that achieving a creamy, scoopable product required iterative testing (roughly six to eight trials). The discussion covers the inevitability of coconut flavor in this base, strategies to push vanilla flavor without overpowering the dessert, and the versatility of the base to accommodate non-vanilla flavors such as coffee, strawberry, or chocolate, making it suitable for lactose-intolerant eaters and others avoiding dairy. The video frames texture and flavor as a middle ground and highlights how dairy-free desserts can still be refreshing and enjoyable while reducing heaviness.
topics: Coconut oil and cocoa butter in vegan ice cream
Vanilla flavor balance with coconut base
Versatility of vegan ice cream bases

sections.title: Texture vs flavor balance
sections.description: Merle discusses the core challenge of balancing texture and flavor in a dairy-free vanilla ice cream, noting that vegan desserts often rely on coconut-based ingredients and that achieving a creamy, scoopable texture without dairy requires navigating a delicate balance between how it tastes and how it feels.

sections.title: Coconut-based base and vanilla balance
concepts: vanilla flavor to counter coconut taste
sections.description: The discussion acknowledges that the base relies on coconut products (coconut milk, coconut oil, cocoa butter) and that coconut flavor is inherently present. Merle emphasizes increasing vanilla to compensate while still aiming for a pleasant texture, and notes the iterative process (six to eight attempts) to optimize both flavor and mouthfeel.

sections.title: Flavor customization and serving ideas
sections.description: Towards the end, Merle highlights that the base can be flavored in many ways beyond vanilla, encouraging experimentation (coffee, strawberry, chocolate) to tailor the ice cream to different tastes while preserving the dairy-free, refreshing nature of the dessert.

featured_techniques.technique: Use a coconut-based base (coconut milk/oil and cocoa butter) to achieve creaminess in dairy-free ice cream
Balance vanilla intensity to counteract coconut flavors (more vanilla without overpowering the product)
Iterative texture testing to avoid soupy or icy results (6-8 trials)
Flavor customization by adding non-vanilla flavors (coffee, strawberry, chocolate)
